transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess the main thing is that my talking has been getting me into trouble, or not trouble exactly, but people look at me like I’ve wandered off somewhere. I work with jewelry, repairs and stones and that sort of thing, and someone will ask me something simple, like, “When will this ring be ready?” and I’ll start answering, but then somehow I’m talking about the invoice, and then the soil in my garden, and then I’m thinking about mortgage papers I need to find, and I can see their face change.

It’s embarrassing, because I know there was a question, and I’m trying to answer it, but my thoughts sort of… branch off. Like I can still see the original road, but I keep taking side streets. And by the time I come back, the customer or whoever asked me is just waiting, and I can tell I’ve lost them. That’s mostly why I came in.
When you're talking and your thoughts branch off like that, do you feel like you're speaking faster than usual or can't keep up with your own thoughts?

Not exactly faster, I don’t think. It’s more like the answer gets… cluttered, if that makes sense. Someone asks me, “When will this ring repair be ready?” and I mean to say, “Thursday” or explain the setting needs one more check, but then I’m talking about the invoice, and the invoice makes me think of paperwork, and then somehow I’m mentioning the soil in my garden, and then mortgage papers I’ve misplaced.

So it isn’t like I’m racing ahead, exactly. I can hear myself going sideways, and I can see the other person’s face change, like they’re trying to follow me but they can’t. I still know there was a simple question at the beginning, but my thoughts keep branching off before I land on the actual answer.
Have you noticed that you’re speaking more than usual, or that you feel a pressure to keep talking even when you might not need to?

I don’t know that I’d call it a pressure, exactly. I mean, I do end up talking more than the situation probably needs, but it doesn’t feel like I’m being pushed from inside to keep going, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that once I start explaining, I keep adding pieces because I’m trying to make it make sense, and then I realize I’ve said too much or gone too far around the barn.

Like at work, if someone asks about a repair, I don’t feel like I have to keep talking just to talk. I’m trying to answer them properly. But then I’ll include the background, and why the timing changed, and something about the stone or the paperwork, and suddenly I’ve given them a whole little tour they didn’t ask for. So… more than usual, maybe in the sense that people seem to notice it, but not like I can’t stop my mouth once it starts. It’s more messy than pressured.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or that others can hear your thoughts?

Not really like someone is putting thoughts in my head, no. And I don’t think people can hear my thoughts exactly. It’s more… I get stuck on what I think they’re really doing.

Like with the new showroom, some customers come in and ask a lot of questions about it — how much work we had done, whether business is picking up, things like that — and I know my husband says they’re just being friendly, making conversation. But sometimes I get very convinced they’re checking on us, like they’re trying to see if I’m going to miss payments or if we’re in trouble financially. I’ll hear a question that maybe sounds harmless, but it feels pointed to me, like they’re not asking out of curiosity, they’re gathering information.

I know that probably sounds odd when I say it out loud. I can see how someone else might say, “They’re just customers admiring the place.” But in the moment it feels very real to me, and I’ll keep watching what they ask and how they look around. So no, not mind-reading exactly, but I do feel like there’s something behind it that other people tell me isn’t there.
Have you ever felt that certain people are working against you or that events in your life are being controlled by others in a way that others don't seem to understand?

Yes… I mean, not like a whole group with a plan, exactly, but I do get that feeling with certain people, especially customers coming into the new showroom.

They’ll ask all these questions — about the renovation, how business has been, whether the new cases were expensive, how long we’ve been there — and I know those can be normal things people ask. My husband keeps telling me they’re just being friendly, that they’re interested because the place looks different. But in my head it starts to feel like they’re not just chatting. It feels like they’re checking up on me, like they’re trying to figure out if we’re stretched too thin or if I’m going to miss payments.

And I know, saying it here, it sounds odd. I can hear that. But when I’m standing there behind the counter and someone keeps asking one question after another, it feels pointed, like there’s a reason behind it that they’re not saying out loud. Then I start watching their face, where they look, what they notice. It’s hard for me to just take it as harmless conversation, even when other people tell me that’s all it is.
Have you ever felt that things people say or do, even things that aren't directed at you, have a special meaning or are about you in some way?

Yes… I think so. Not every little thing, but there are times when something someone says feels like it’s really about me, even if they don’t come right out and say that.

It happens mostly in the showroom. Since we redid it, people will come in and say things like, “Oh, this must have been a big project,” or “Business must be doing well,” or they’ll ask how long we’ve been there, whether we changed all the cases, things like that. And I know those are normal questions. My husband says they’re just being friendly, that people notice the new space and they’re making conversation.

But sometimes it starts to feel like there’s a second meaning underneath it. Like they’re not really asking about the showroom — they’re checking whether we spent too much, or whether I’m going to fall behind, or whether payments are going to be missed. I’ll hear a question and it feels pointed, like it’s aimed at something they shouldn’t even know about.

I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud. I can see that maybe I’m reading too much into it. But in the moment, when someone keeps asking one thing after another, it’s hard not to feel like it’s about me and whether I’m handling things right.
Have you ever felt that certain things people say or do are directed at you, even if they don’t seem to be, or that your thoughts are being influenced or controlled by outside forces?

Yes, I’ve felt that way about things being directed at me, mostly with customers in the showroom. I don’t really mean my thoughts are being controlled from outside — it’s not like that, exactly. But I do get very caught up in what people say, and it starts to feel like it’s aimed at me.

Like since we redid the showroom, some people come in and ask what seems like too many questions — how much we changed, whether business has picked up, if it was expensive, things like that. My husband tells me they’re just being friendly and curious, and I know that makes sense. But in the moment I can get convinced they’re actually checking on us, or checking on me, to see if I’m going to miss payments or if we’re in trouble.

I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud. I can hear that. But when they keep asking questions, it doesn’t feel harmless to me. It feels like there’s something behind it, like they’re trying to find out something they’re not saying directly.
Have you ever felt that certain events, like something happening on TV or something someone said in another conversation, were specifically directed at you or had a special meaning for you alone?

Not so much with TV, no… I don’t really sit there thinking a news story or a show is secretly talking to me. It’s more when someone is actually in front of me, talking, especially in the showroom.

Like I said, since we redid it, people come in and they’ll ask all these questions — about the cases, how long the work took, whether business is better, things like that. And I know people do that. I know a renovated place makes people curious. My husband keeps saying, “They’re just being friendly, they’re making conversation,” and part of me understands that.

But then if they keep asking, I start feeling like it isn’t just casual. It starts to feel like they’re really trying to find out if we spent too much, or if I’m going to miss payments, or if something is wrong financially. I can get pretty convinced of that in the moment, even though when I say it out loud it sounds… I don’t know, like I’m making too much of it. But it feels directed at me, like there’s a meaning underneath what they’re saying that only I’m picking up on.

Have you ever felt that random events, like something happening in the environment or something someone else said in passing, were specifically about you or had a hidden personal meaning meant only for you, even if others didn’t see it that way?

Yes… I mean, not so much like a bird landing outside or something on the radio has a message for me. It’s more with people saying things in passing, especially customers at the store.

I know I’ve probably said this already, but the showroom has been the big thing. Since we changed it, people come in and make comments like, “Oh, this looks expensive,” or “You must be doing well,” or they ask how much work we had done, whether business is better now, whether it took a long time. And I know, logically, those are normal things to ask. My husband tells me that all the time — that they’re just being friendly, that people notice the new cases and the lighting and they’re just making conversation.

But when it’s one question after another, I start feeling like there’s something underneath it. Like they’re not really asking about the showroom. It feels like they’re checking on whether we spent too much, or whether I’m going to miss payments, or whether we’re in trouble somehow. I can get pretty convinced of that while it’s happening, even if nobody else sees it that way.

And then later I’ll think, “Why would they know anything about that?” or “Maybe they were just chatting.” But in the moment, it feels personal. It feels aimed at me, like there’s a hidden meaning in what they’re saying. I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud, but that’s how it feels.

But when it’s one question after another, I start feeling like there’s something underneath it. Like they’re not really asking about the showroom. It feels like they’re checking on whether we spent too much, or whether I’m going to miss payments, or whether we’re in trouble somehow. I can get pretty convinced of that while it’s happening, even if nobody else sees it that way.

And then later I’ll think, “Why would they know anything about that?” or “Maybe they were just chatting.” But in the moment, it feels personal. It feels aimed at me, like there’s a hidden meaning in what they’re saying. I know it sounds odd when I say it out loud, but that’s how it feels.
